Fort William is where Scotland shows off — and where my emergency snacks got their most scenic workout of the trip.

Honest numbers first: Fort William scored 5/10 on my GF safety scale, my lowest Scotland score, and no restaurant broke 3/5. This is a scenery-first, food-second town. Fortunately, the scenery is not messing around:

→ Ben Nevis — the UK's tallest mountain, and the whole reason you're here. I hiked it on one of those rare days when the clouds stayed below the path: Loch Linnhe glittering on one side, Fort William spread out underneath. Get a clear day and it's the best seat in Scotland.
→ Browns — the restaurant at the Nevis Bank Inn, best of my Fort William bunch at 3/5. The GF chocolate tart is the headliner — my notes from the night just say "incredible," which from me is basically a standing ovation.
→ Where I stayed: Nevis Bank Inn — after a mountain day, the shortest possible distance between you and dinner is a feature, not a compromise. Booking link is in the guide.
→ The Geographer — 3/5, lively spot on the high street, and the place my guide sends you for GF calamari.

Also in the full guide: three more researched GF options, the Glenfinnan Viaduct (yes, the Harry Potter one — researched, admired from my laptop, still counts), and Crannog at Garrison West, the one that got away and is top of my list for next time.

The full Fort William guide — all 5 restaurants with honest GF scores, the hotel, and a map — is on the site (link in bio). Verdict: come for the mountain, pack the snacks. That's not a warning; in Fort William, it's just the itinerary.
